calls.summary: Maria Gonzalez called asking for same-day access to start Suboxone treatment at the nearest clinic. Agent Lila confirmed an open same-day intake slot, verified her location, and walked her through what to bring. Maria scheduled her new patient intake appointment for that afternoon.

David Ramirez wanted to begin methadone maintenance and asked whether his Medicaid plan would cover the program. Agent Mary confirmed his coverage was accepted and explained daily dispensing. David booked a new patient intake appointment and felt reassured about cost.

Angela Brooks called to ask about the Vivitrol shot cost and whether Medicaid would pay for the monthly injection. Agent Oscar explained the naltrexone program and coverage details clearly. Angela wanted to discuss it with family first and did not schedule an intake appointment yet.

Robert Chen called as a new patient to start methadone treatment and asked how the intake process works. Agent Rosey collected his contact details, insurance information, and preferred clinic, then explained the medical evaluation and care plan. Robert scheduled his new patient intake appointment for the next morning.

Latoya Jackson reached out for help with heroin dependence and asked about same-day access to care. Agent Lee confirmed a same-day opening and reviewed the MAT program with counseling included. Latoya booked her intake appointment and thanked the agent for the quick response.

Michael Turner called to reschedule an existing group counseling session because of a work conflict. Agent Sue found a later slot the same week and updated his record. This was an existing patient scheduling change, so no new intake appointment was created.

Sarah Nguyen was deciding between Suboxone and a Vivitrol program and wanted guidance on which fit her situation. Agent Mike explained the differences and helped her choose to start with an assessment. Sarah scheduled a new patient intake appointment to begin treatment.

Kevin O'Brien disputed a self-pay charge on his monthly statement that he believed was already covered. Agent Jennifer reviewed the billing history and opened a case for the finance team to investigate. Kevin remained frustrated and no appointment was booked.

Priya Patel called about co-occurring anxiety alongside her opioid use disorder and asked if both could be treated together. Agent Rose explained the dual diagnosis approach and available counseling. Priya scheduled a new patient intake appointment despite some hesitation about the wait.

Thomas Reed complained that his take-home methadone doses were delayed and he could not reach his clinic. Agent Oscar apologized, checked the dispensing notes, and escalated to the clinic manager. Thomas stayed upset and this was a service issue, not a new intake.

Jessica Moore called to cancel an upcoming intake appointment because she found a clinic closer to home. Agent Lila confirmed the cancellation and offered to transfer her records. No new appointment was scheduled on this call.

Brandon Cole complained about long wait times in the dosing line and inconsistent counseling schedules. Agent Lee listened and logged the feedback for the clinic director. Brandon was dissatisfied and did not book anything new.

Denise Walker left a voicemail after hours asking whether recent Medicaid changes would affect her coverage and cost. The call rolled to voicemail and no agent answered. A callback was queued but nothing was scheduled.

Gregory Adams angrily disputed a charge and said his insurance should have covered his Suboxone visit fees. Agent Jennifer tried to explain the self-pay balance but he interrupted repeatedly. The call ended without resolution and no appointment.

Nicole Foster complained that her counselor kept changing and she felt no continuity in her care. Agent Sue apologized and offered to note the concern, but Nicole remained frustrated. She hung up without scheduling any follow up.

prompts.question: Is the customer trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes. The caller is struggling with fentanyl dependence and seeking medication-assisted treatment to stabilize and reduce cravings. They want to know if same-day or near-immediate intake is possible.

prompts.question: What are the customer's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller expects a non-judgmental environment, quick access to treatment without long waitlists, and clear guidance on what happens at their first intake appointment.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: Marcus could have captured the caller's email address for appointment confirmation, explained what documents or insurance information to bring, and explicitly mentioned the combination of medication plus counseling that is part of BHG's integrated model.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Behavioral Health Group. This is Marcus speaking. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi, yes, I'm looking for help with opioid addiction. I'm using fentanyl and I'm ready to get treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm really glad you reached out. You're calling the right place. We specialize in medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder. Can I get your name first?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's Jennifer. Jennifer Martinez.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Jennifer. How long have you been struggling with fentanyl use?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: About two years now. It started with pain medication and then switched to street fentanyl. I need help.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Jennifer, I hear you, and I'm glad you're taking this step. We have programs specifically for fentanyl addiction, and we offer medications like buprenorphine or methadone combined with counseling. What city or area are you calling from?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I'm in the Denver area. Is that somewhere you serve?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. We have a clinic in Denver that can see you very soon. Do you have a phone number where we can reach you to confirm your appointment?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. And Jennifer, have you thought about whether you'd prefer to use insurance or self-pay for your treatment?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I have Medicaid. Will that work?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely. Medicaid covers our treatment. I'm going to schedule you for an intake appointment this Friday at 10 AM at our Denver clinic. You'll meet with our intake specialist, and we'll do a full medical evaluation and get you started on a medication plan. Is that day and time okay?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, Friday at 10 AM works great. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome, Jennifer. We look forward to seeing you. Have a good day.

callDetail.aiSummary: Jennifer Martinez called seeking medication-assisted treatment for fentanyl use disorder after two years of struggling with addiction that began with prescription opioids. Marcus Bell confirmed BHG serves the Denver area, gathered Jennifer's contact information, and scheduled her for a Friday 10 AM intake appointment at the Denver clinic. Jennifer has Medicaid coverage, which Marcus confirmed is accepted. The call was professional and welcoming, though Marcus did not capture Jennifer's email address or provide detailed information about what to bring to her appointment or the full integrated treatment model combining medication and counseling.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, great opening and solid warmth with Jennifer. You did an excellent job acknowledging her courage and confirming our location immediately. Two coaching notes for next time, please. First, always capture an email address so we can send appointment details and pre-intake forms electronically. Second, take 30 more seconds to briefly explain what to expect at intake and what documents she should bring, especially since this is her first time with BHG. This sets expectation and reduces no-shows. You did handle the insurance question well. Well done.

transcript.text: Hi, um, I've never done anything like this before. I've been using fentanyl and I really need to get some help before it gets worse.

transcript.text: I'm really glad you called, and I want you to know you did the right thing reaching out. Can I start with your first and last name?

transcript.text: Yeah, it's Daniel Foster.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Daniel. And so I can point you to the right care, how long have you been using and are you dealing with any withdrawal right now?

transcript.text: About two years now. The withdrawals hit hard if I stop, that's honestly what keeps pulling me back in.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That is exactly what our Fentanyl Addiction Treatment Program addresses. Most patients start on a medication like buprenorphine, our Suboxone program, paired with counseling to steady the cravings and stop the withdrawal cycle.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there. This is Sarah from Behavioral Health Group. We help people with substance use disorders get access to medication and counseling. Do you or someone you care about need help with addiction treatment?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, I've been struggling with opioids for a while now. I want to get clean but I don't know where to start.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm really glad you reached out. We can help. Are you currently using any medications like methadone, buprenorphine, or anything else to manage cravings?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: No, I'm not on anything. I've just been trying to quit on my own but it's not working.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That takes courage. Many people find that medication combined with counseling is the most effective path. Have you ever heard of buprenorphine or Suboxone?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: I've heard of Suboxone. Isn't that expensive?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Suboxone treatment typically runs between 150 and 400 dollars per month depending on your dosing, plus visit fees. Most of our patients use Medicaid, Medicare, or commercial insurance though. Do you have insurance?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, I have Medicaid. That should cover it right?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great. Medicaid covers our treatment programs. I'd like to get you started with a new patient intake and assessment. That's a medical evaluation where we create a care plan for you. We have same day appointments available. Are mornings or afternoons better for you?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Mornings work better for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. We have an opening tomorrow, March 11th at 9:30 AM at our clinic. Does that work for you?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, that works. What do I need to bring?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Just bring a photo ID and your Medicaid card. Your appointment is scheduled for tomorrow March 11th at 9:30 AM. You'll speak with our medical team who will evaluate you and discuss your treatment options. If you need to reach us before then, call 877-936-2933. Looking forward to helping you on your recovery journey.

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Thank you so much. I really appreciate this.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Behavioral Health Group. This is Marcus. Are you calling about medication assisted treatment or one of our other recovery programs today?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, hi. I'm dealing with a fentanyl addiction and I've heard you guys can help with same day treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad you reached out. We absolutely can help, and many of our patients do start treatment the same day they call. Just so I understand your situation better, have you ever been through addiction treatment before?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: No, this is my first time looking for help.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay, that's helpful to know. A lot of our new patients start with an intake assessment where we'll talk about your history and get you set up with one of our evidence based medications. Do you have insurance, or would you be self pay?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: I have Medicaid. Does that cover it?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, Medicaid covers our medication assisted treatment programs in most cases. Your out of pocket costs would be minimal or none depending on your state. Have you already decided which medication you'd prefer, like buprenorphine, or would you want to discuss options at your intake appointment?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: I'm not sure. What would you recommend for fentanyl?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: For fentanyl addiction, we typically recommend buprenorphine or naltrexone. Buprenorphine is a partial agonist, so it's office based with take home dosing once you're stable. Naltrexone is a non narcotic blocker with no misuse potential. Your doctor will help you choose at intake. Can you come in tomorrow morning at ten AM?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning works. Yeah, that's perfect.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Let me confirm your appointment. That's tomorrow, January 16th at 10 AM for your new patient intake assessment. We're located at 452 Commerce Drive in Denver. Please plan to spend about an hour with us. Do you have any questions before we hang up?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: No, I think I'm good. Thanks a lot.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome. We're really glad you called. If you need to reschedule or have any questions before your appointment, just call us back at 877-936-2933. We'll see you tomorrow at 10 AM.

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Great, thank you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Take care.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask only one question per message, covering which substance or addiction they need help with, whether this is for themselves or a loved one, which medication or treatment they are interested in (methadone, buprenorphine/Suboxone, or Vivitrol), their insurance or payment method (Medicaid, Medicare, commercial, or self-pay), their availability, and their ZIP code to confirm a nearby accredited center.

Confirm then book: Confirm there is a Joint Commission-accredited BHG center serving their ZIP code, explain that costs are typically covered by Medicaid, Medicare, or commercial insurance and that a specialist will review coverage during intake, propose a specific same-day or next-day intake appointment time, and confirm they will receive a reminder text with a clinic phone number to call before the appointment.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer same-day treatment?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, most patients begin treatment right away with same-day access to care and no waitlists. I can set up an intake appointment for you today at a nearby center.

qaPairs.question: What medications do you use for opioid addiction?
qaPairs.answer: We offer FDA-approved medications including methadone, buprenorphine/Suboxone, and naltrexone/Vivitrol, combined with counseling and support. A specialist will recommend the best option for you during your intake appointment.

qaPairs.question: Do you take Medicaid?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, most of our care is billed to Medicaid, Medicare, or commercial insurance, and our team can verify your coverage. Let me get you scheduled so a specialist can confirm your benefits.

qaPairs.question: How much does treatment cost?
qaPairs.answer: Costs vary based on your treatment plan and insurance, and most patients pay little to nothing out of pocket with coverage. A specialist will review exact costs with you at your intake appointment, so let me get you scheduled.

qaPairs.question: Where is the closest clinic to me?
qaPairs.answer: We have 110+ accredited centers across 20+ states, so there is likely one near you. Share your ZIP code and I will confirm the closest center and book your intake.

qaPairs.question: What is methadone treatment?
qaPairs.answer: Methadone is a daily dispensed medication that acts on the same brain receptors as opioids to reduce cravings and stabilize brain chemistry. A provider can explain if it is right for you at your intake appointment.

qaPairs.question: What is the difference between Suboxone and methadone?
qaPairs.answer: Suboxone is a partial-agonist option with lower overdose risk and possible take-home dosing, while methadone is a daily dispensed full agonist. Our specialists will help you choose the best fit during intake.

qaPairs.question: Can you help with fentanyl addiction?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we have a condition-specific medication protocol for high-potency synthetic opioid dependence like fentanyl. I can book you an intake appointment to get started.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat heroin addiction?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer targeted maintenance and counseling pathways for heroin use disorder. Let me schedule your intake appointment so you can begin care.

qaPairs.question: Can you help with kratom or 7-OH withdrawal?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we have a program that addresses kratom withdrawal symptoms, timeline, and treatment options. I can set up an intake appointment to get you support.

qaPairs.question: What happens at the new patient intake?
qaPairs.answer: Intake includes a medical evaluation, care planning, and an introduction to our services and medications. I can book that appointment for you now, often same day.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer counseling too?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide individual and group counseling alongside medication as part of our integrated model. You can meet with a counselor as part of your treatment plan set up at intake.

qaPairs.question: What is an Intensive Outpatient Program?
qaPairs.answer: Our IOP offers structured multi-hour weekly programming for higher-acuity needs while you continue living at home. A specialist can determine if IOP is right for you at your intake appointment.

qaPairs.question: Is treatment confidential?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, your care and information are kept private and handled by our licensed professionals. Let me schedule a confidential intake appointment for you.

qaPairs.question: Can I get treatment for a family member?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we help patients and their loved ones get started with care. Share a few details and I can book an intake appointment for them.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat co-occurring mental health conditions?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer dual-diagnosis care that addresses substance use alongside conditions like anxiety and depression. A provider will assess your needs during intake.

qaPairs.question: Do I need an appointment or can I walk in?
qaPairs.answer: You can call or walk in, and most patients begin treatment right away with same-day access. I can also book an intake appointment now to make your visit smoother.

qaPairs.question: What is Vivitrol?
qaPairs.answer: Vivitrol is a non-narcotic monthly injection that blocks opioids with no misuse potential. A specialist can discuss whether it fits your plan at your intake appointment.

qaPairs.question: Are your clinics accredited?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we are the largest network of Joint Commission-accredited outpatient treatment centers in the United States. I can book your intake at an accredited center near you.

qaPairs.question: How do I get started?
qaPairs.answer: Getting started is easy and often same day. Just share your ZIP code and preferred time and I will book your intake appointment at the nearest center.
